errors.stored: [sodium chloride, calcium chloride, sodium lactate, magnesium chloride, icodextrin]
errors.should_be: [icodextrin]. WRONG (extra components): the application lists only icodextrin as its active ingredient. The four electrolytes are dialysate background components. They are not the application's active ingredient, and sodium lactate also keeps its salt form.

errors.item: line 100, NDA 209589, ingredients [CITRIC ACID; MAGNESIUM OXIDE; SODIUM PICOSULFATE] (Clenpiq)
errors.should_be: [citric acid, magnesium oxide, picosulfate]. WRONG (salt not stripped): sodium is a counterion; the FDA active moiety is picosulfate. The same file strips sodium from SODIUM NITROPRUSSIDE to give nitroprusside (line 63), so keeping 'sodium picosulfate' breaks the file's own policy. Citric acid and magnesium oxide are inorganic or acid actives and are correctly kept whole.

[clobetasol]. ACCEPTABLE: an ester is not a salt, so the stored name holds up under the strict 'salts stripped' rule. However, the file strips esters everywhere else, following the FDA active-moiety convention: halobetasol propionate becomes halobetasol (line 50), cortisone acetate becomes cortisone (line 22), triamcinolone diacetate becomes triamcinolone (line 40) and estradiol valerate becomes estradiol (line 53). For consistency this should be clobetasol.

[hyaluronidase human recombinant] (rHuPH20). ACCEPTABLE: the entity is right, but dropping 'human recombinant' merges this product with the bovine (Amphadase) and ovine (Vitrase) hyaluronidases, which are different proteins. The file keeps similar distinctions elsewhere, e.g. interferon beta-1a.

notes:
I formed my own answer for each line before reading the stored moieties. 96 lines are correct. The most common pattern is a salt correctly stripped: hydrochloride, sulfate, sodium, fumarate, mesylate, besylate, maleate, malate, lactate, tosylate, napsylate, benzathine (line 52 gives benzylpenicillin) and disodium (line 28 gives carbenicillin). Biologic and biosimilar suffixes are also correctly dropped: -lanm, -ipdl, -dssb and -adet. Combination products list every component and nothing extra (lines 35, 43, 53, 66, 67, 68, 70, 73, 77, 87, 90). 

Line 42 (Cenestin, synthetic conjugated estrogens A) correctly expands to the nine sodium sulfate-conjugate estrogens in its label. The sodium is stripped and the covalent sulfate is kept, which is right. 

Line 77 keeps sodium bicarbonate whole, which is right because the inorganic salt is itself the active ingredient. Line 76 keeps 'baloxavir marboxil', which is the INN of the approved prodrug and counts as correct. Line 11 (Tc-99m medronate kit) and line 5 (Lu-177 dotatate) are reasonable radiopharmaceutical normalizations. 

The file has an ester-stripping policy that is applied unevenly: line 31 keeps the propionate while lines 22, 40, 50 and 53 strip their esters. If the pipeline intends FDA active-moiety semantics (21 CFR 314.3), only line 31 needs changing. If it intends 'salts only', then lines 22, 40, 50 and 53 would need to keep their esters instead. I followed the FDA active-moiety reading. No files were modified.

notes:
Judgments formed from the letter text before reading the stored uses; every line counted once (indices are 0-based). Result: 55 correct, 5 partially (all reported in n_acceptable), 0 wrong.

1) All 5 errors are the same pattern: an extra efficacy_labeling row on a labeling-only letter (lines 9, 27, 42, 43, 58). The rubric says a labeling-only letter should have no uses, so each is an extra use. The extraction prompt (pipeline/fda.py LETTER_SYSTEM) explicitly allows an efficacy_labeling change_type for 'efficacy data added to labeling without a new population'. The model followed its own schema, and the schema conflicts with the rubric. Either filter change_type='efficacy_labeling' out of anything treated as an approved use, or drop that category from the prompt. Elsewhere the model correctly returned empty uses for labeling-only letters (1, 23, 27 excepted, 36, 41, 48, 57, 59).

2) Truncated source text (counted correct, but a real data gap): lines 12 (sha 3de1d61842f8, Imjudo BLA 761289 original approval) and 52 (sha cbbc9d90247d, Asparlas BLA 761102 original approval). The stored letter_text starts on page 3 and page 2, so the indication paragraph is missing. Empty uses is the faithful extraction, but the DB will lack the true original-approval rows (Imjudo: unresectable HCC with durvalumab; Asparlas: ALL). The source PDF text extraction should be re-fetched.

3) Borderline calls accepted as correct:
- Line 2: Steqeyma interchangeability (BLA Original 2) lists the 6 indications as change_type=other. Reasonable, since these uses were first approved in the Dec 2024 biosimilarity letter.
- Line 20: Jylamvo pJIA stored as new_population. pJIA was not on the adult label, but the letter frames it as a pediatric expansion and PREA says the new-indication criteria do not apply.
- Line 22: Daklinza second row (HCV GT3 with HIV coinfection, new_regimen). It covers added dosing recommendations; acceptable.
- Line 38: Opdivo flat-dose change for cHL and SCCHN as new_regimen. Matches the schema, and PREA applied as a new dosing regimen.
- Lines 0 and 35: new-dosage-form NDAs (Promacta oral suspension, Trikafta oral granules) stored as original_approval, per the schema's ORIG rule.

Only disease and change_type were judged; qualifiers were not scored. No files were modified, and the DB credentials in the user message were not used (not needed).
